A VibeApp is an application that your colleagues or your customers use, with one or several of your Agentivity teams working behind it. The people who use it never see the Studio.

## What it looks like for the person who uses it

1. **They ask in their own words.** One sentence is enough: what they need, with the details they have.
2. **A team works on it.** Behind the screen, the right specialists take each part of the request.
3. **The screens arrive when they are needed.** When a choice is needed, the application shows it: a list of options, a card, a form. There is no fixed sequence of forms to fill in first.
4. **They decide.** When a decision is theirs, the team stops and waits. What they choose changes what comes next.
5. **They receive finished work.**

Trip Planner, one of the Agentivity showcases, is a VibeApp. A traveller writes one sentence: a city, the dates, the budget. A manager sends the flights, the hotel, the transfers and the dinner to different specialists. The traveller chooses among the options. You can watch it on the [use cases](/use-cases) page of the website.

## What is behind a VibeApp

- **Your solutions.** The agents, teams and workflows that you built in the Studio. The application only starts them and shows what they do.
- **Your Agentivity server.** The application talks to it. Your data stays there.
- **The Agentivity SDK.** A set of ready-made parts for developers: the conversation, the choices, the forms, the charts. SDK means software development kit.

## What a VibeApp is not

- **It is not a chatbot.** A chatbot answers. A VibeApp gets a request handled from start to finish, and shows real screens when a text answer is not enough.
- **It is not the Studio.** Nobody builds or changes a team from a VibeApp. Building stays in the Studio.
- **It is not required.** Most of the time you need no application: you can run a solution straight from the Studio. See [One app for one job, or one portal for all your teams](/docs/vibeapps/one-app-or-one-portal/).

## Who makes a VibeApp

- **A person who knows the job** builds the solution in the Studio, with or without the Assistant.
- **A developer** builds the application around it with the SDK. If you use the ready-made portal, there is very little to develop.
